text:
julia (Acme): Hi — our account just went negative after a refund/chargeback. We had $100 in trial credits and a $20 promo applied; after a chargeback the balance now shows -$120 and API calls return 402 Payment Required. Can someone help?

maria - support: Sorry about that, Julia. Can you share your account ID or the last 4 of the invoice so we can look up the transaction?

julia (Acme): acct_87Ght, invoice #INV-3421 last4 3421. Chargeback was submitted by their bank, refunded $140 on 2026-02-25. Trial credits were used earlier this month.

maria - support: Got it — I'm pulling the ledger now. Noted the refund posted overnight. Quick question: are you seeing any specific error payload from the API call?

julia (Acme): Example response: `{ "error": { "message": "Payment required: insufficient funds", "code": 402 } }` — It happens on both generation and embeddings endpoints.

simon - eng: tagging in. 402 is our billing rejection path. Likely the chargeback caused a reversal of applied credits which drove the balance negative. Can you confirm whether the refund was processed as a reversal or a manual refund?

alex - billing: I can confirm refund shows as a chargeback (dispute) on our side — code CHBK. Our current policy automatically clawbacks any promotional/trial credits tied to transactions that are refunded or charged back. That can create a negative balance if payments were already offset by credits.

julia (Acme): So the customer disputes a charge and our credits get pulled back from the account? That seems harsh — their product didn't change.

alex - billing: I hear you. The clawback exists to avoid subsidizing disputed charges. But in this case the timing looks like the trial/promo credits were used earlier to pay for usage, then the chargeback removed the original payment and the system removed the credits, leaving a net negative. We can escalate.

maria - support: For immediate relief we can do a temporary credit grant to bring you to $0 so API resumes. Would you like that while we investigate permanent fixes?

julia (Acme): Yes please — API is in production for us. A temporary credit would help.

alex - billing: I'll apply a $140 temporary credit and mark it as 'billing-emergency'. Doing: `admin credits adjust --acct acct_87Ght --amount +140 --reason "temp restore after CHBK"`

support-bot: Action completed: temporary credit +$140 applied to acct_87Ght by alex - billing at 2026-02-26 09:10 UTC.

julia (Acme): Thanks! API calls are working again. Can you also explain next steps so this doesn't happen repeatedly?

alex - billing: We're going to: 1) make the credit-clawback process more conservative for trial/promo grants (don't clawback <= $X or within Y days), 2) add clearer ledger entries so you can see what triggered the negative amount, 3) provide an option for manual review before clawback on disputed charges. I'll open an internal change ticket.

simon - eng: From the runtime side, I'll create a small change to return a clearer error when 402 triggers with negative balance, include balance and link to billing console. Right now the message is generic. That should make it easier to triage.

maria - support: Filed INC-5243 to track billing escalation + temporary credit. Alex, Simon — can you add ETA?

alex - billing: I'll have a billing policy proposal by EOD Fri, will include thresholds.

simon - eng: I'll put a tiny API change on next sprint, estimate 1 week for rollout.

julia (Acme): Appreciate it. One last question — will the temporary credit be removed if the chargeback later resolves in our favor?

alex - billing: Good question. We'll mark it non-reversible until the dispute closes; if the dispute resolves for you, we can convert the temp credit to permanent or remove it as needed.

maria - support: Closing loop: temp credit applied, engineering + billing investigating policy/ticket. We'll follow up in this thread with updates. Thanks for reporting. :thumbsup: 

julia (Acme): Perfect, thanks everyone.
